title: Kashmir Route Outpaces Manali as Ladakh Tourism Hits 98% of 2025 Total by July
excerpt: Ladakh recorded over 330,000 tourists in seven months, driven by a road network that has more than doubled since 2019 and dramatically reduced seasonal closures.
body:
• Ladakh recorded 330,332 tourists from January to July 2026, reaching 98.35% of the entire 2025 total with five months still remaining.
  • The Kashmir route accounts for 35.27% of road arrivals, outpacing the Manali route at 17.09%, while air travel remains the top mode at 47.64%.
  • Road infrastructure has more than doubled since 2019, from 1,799 km to over 4,200 km, with Zoji La closures shrinking from 127 days to just 16.
  • Homestays have surged from 128 in 2019 to 2,275 in 2026, creating livelihood opportunities for local households.

Ladakh has recorded 330,332 tourist arrivals between January and July 2026, already reaching 98.35% of the 335,872 tourists the union territory saw in all of 2025, according to figures released by the Ladakh government.

June and July alone accounted for more than 212,000 visitors — nearly 65% of the year's total — as improved infrastructure and a packed cultural calendar pulled travelers to the high-altitude region.

Kashmir Route Pulls Ahead

Among tourists arriving by road, the Kashmir route continued to dominate, with 35.27% of visitors entering Ladakh through Kashmir compared with 17.09% through Manali. Air travel remained the most popular mode overall, accounting for 47.64% of total arrivals.

The shift toward the Kashmir route reflects a dramatic reduction in seasonal disruptions. Zoji La, the gateway to Ladakh from Kashmir, now remains closed for only 16 days annually, down from approximately 127 days before the union territory's formation. The Kargil-Zanskar Road's annual closure has similarly dropped from 154 days to just 11.

A Connectivity Transformation

The tourism surge coincides with rapid infrastructure development. Ladakh's total road network has expanded from 1,799 km in 2019 to over 4,200 km in 2026, while the number of bridges has increased from 19 to 72, according to the government.

The homestay sector has seen explosive growth, jumping from 128 registered homestays in 2019 to 2,275 in 2026. The expansion has created livelihood opportunities for local households in remote communities that previously had limited economic options.

"The fact that Ladakh has crossed the 1 lakh mark in tourist arrivals for two successive months and has already achieved more than 98% of the entire 2025 footfall by the end of July is a very encouraging milestone."

— Vinai Kumar Saxena, Lieutenant Governor of Ladakh

What Is Drawing Visitors

A government spokesperson attributed the surge in June and July arrivals to a calendar of cultural, spiritual, and experiential events organised across Ladakh. Lieutenant Governor Vinai Kumar Saxena credited the sustained infrastructure development and Prime Minister Modi's appeals to citizens to visit domestic tourist destinations.

What NRI Travelers Should Know

For diaspora travelers planning a Ladakh trip, the data points to an increasingly accessible destination. The Kashmir route via Srinagar offers more reliable access with shorter closure windows, while direct flights now serve as the primary entry point. The rapid growth in homestays provides accommodation options beyond traditional hotels, though the spike in visitor numbers — particularly during June and July — suggests advance booking is advisable during peak monsoon-season months.

At the current pace, Ladakh appears on track to significantly exceed its 2025 visitor total by year-end, signaling a structural shift in the region's tourism economy rather than a one-off seasonal bump.
